Madam Speaker, my question is for the Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources. Has the Alsands consortium indicated to him at what point in time, if negotiations are not completed, the Alsands project will fall by the pulling out of the remaining companies? If the negotiations are not complete, does the minister have a target date in mind that the Alsands consortium will not proceed?

BasePK: 3345023
Chunk index: 0

Speech chunk:
I can assure hon. members that I will do everything I can in this matter and, further to that, I have already asked my department to examine the possibility of reinforcing the air rescue capabilities in Newfoundland as much as possible, without disrupting the effectiveness of other areas. As for the recommendations in 1970, to which the hon. member referred, as I said yesterday, a lot has been done as far as improvements to our search and rescue capabilities over the last few years. As I said yesterday, we have initiated many improvements for our helicopters, such as providing long-range fuel tanks, rescue hoists, high-powered search lights, and some improved navigational avionics. In addition, we are currently working on new radar and improved instrumentation. Therefore I think a lot has been done about improving our search and rescue capabilities.

I should like to deal briefly with the main objectives of the proposal introduced by the minister. First of all, it sets out to abandon the existing statutory freight rate; it commits the government to a level of funding equal to the 1981-82 railway revenue shortfall and it calls upon producers to meet any future cost increases beyond the 1981-82 shortfall in negotiation with the railways. One must pause and think about that, Mr. Speaker. What chance would producers have to negotiate freight rates with the railways? That would Transportation be very, very difficult indeed. Large corporations have tried to tackle the railways in an effort to gain a fair freight rate and have not succeeded. That is a serious weakness in the proposal.
